verdict.rationale: LiteLLM logs proxy inputs, outputs and exceptions to many backends (Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, S3, DataDog and others). It gives each request a unique call_id and tracks spend metadata per request, even when message content is redacted. However, the evidence never says latency or token counts are attached to logged entries. Inspection appears to depend on external logging providers rather than a documented built-in request log viewer. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of per-request latency and token counts in logs, a documented in-product view for browsing logged requests and responses, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
